clue.text: Potential weapon for rampaging Viking going to France

indicators.note: rampaging raiders charge about wildly, so the letters that follow are scattered into a fresh order

parts.note: the country taken as written, going along with the Norseman

explanation.surface: A Norse raider crossing the Channel to France, armed and ready to cause havoc.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade for slicing the Sunday joint could serve as a weapon in a pinch, hence only potential.

clue.text: Emitter of smoke ring concealing name unknown

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hold it hidden inside, so the bell sound wraps around the next piece

parts.note: to ring a bell is to chime
N is the abbreviation for name
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: A smoke ring hiding some anonymous figure, as if in a detective puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring looks like a noun shaped by smoke, but it is the verb for a bell sounding; unknown is the algebraic letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A flue on a rooftop lets out the smoke rising from a fire or furnace below.

clue.text: Wake up to serial killer's fifth mutilation

indicators.note: a mutilated body is cut about and rearranged, so the letters are put in another order
fifth points to a single letter, counted along from the start of the word it qualifies

explanation.surface: Waking to news of a serial murderer's fifth gruesome attack.
explanation.walkthrough: Serial here belongs to the fodder, not to the killer; only the killer's fifth letter joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: To become aware of a fact is to come to recognise it, much as one finally grasps a situation.

clue.text: Musical Rice and I mount is not very original

indicators.note: in a down entry, to mount is to climb upwards, so the whole sequence is read from the bottom

parts.note: the Lloyd Webber and Rice show about Eva Peron

explanation.surface: A claim that a musical by Rice and the speaker's own staging lack originality.
explanation.walkthrough: Tim Rice wrote the lyrics for this Lloyd Webber show, which is why the setter can pair the two words in one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something copied from another work lacks originality, so it is derivative rather than new.

clue.text: Twelve dozen is just too much!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a quantity of one hundred and forty-four

explanation.surface: Someone exclaiming that a hundred and forty-four of something is simply excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names 144 items as a trade quantity and, in slang, describes anything revolting or excessive.

clue.text: Acquires information about rising savings

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from bottom to top
about means surrounding here, so the word for information goes round the verb

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone learning about rising savings rates, gathering facts on their investments.
explanation.walkthrough: Rising looks like it describes the savings, but in a down entry it tells you to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum put aside over time for the future is a reserve fund, likened to a nest egg left to encourage laying.

clue.text: Formed ranks with top Italian director

parts.note: soldiers fell in when they formed ranks on parade

indicators.note: in a down entry the top of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Troops lining up beside an Italian film-maker of the highest class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top Italian director' reads as one phrase, but top just takes the first letter and director alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Fellini was the celebrated Italian film-maker behind La Dolce Vita and 8 1/2.

clue.text: Tory getting prize money is above being lecherous

parts.note: taken as written, placed above the money in the down entry

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician collecting prize money and lusting after more, a lecherous scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'above' means earlier in the word, so the clue's last piece goes before the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Concupiscent means full of sexual desire, a formal word for lustful.

clue.text: Order to include capital "I" in paperwork

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so the honour wraps around the city

parts.note: the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An instruction to write a capital letter I somewhere in a set of documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital I' looks like a single upper-case letter; capital is a city on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese craft of folding sheets into shapes, so it is quite literally work with paper.

clue.text: Growth of large steel refinery

parts.note: OS is outsize, the clothing label for large

indicators.note: a refinery processes raw material into a new form, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Expansion at a big steelworks.
explanation.definitionFit: An osselet is a bony outgrowth on a horse's leg, often around the fetlock joint.

clue.text: Examiner covering drunken sot's unique hormone

indicators.note: to cover is to go around the outside, so the examiner encloses the jumbled word
a drunk staggers about out of order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An inspector shielding a drunkard with some unique hormone problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Testosterone is the principal male sex hormone, produced chiefly in the testes.

clue.text: Twice preserve a bar

parts.note: two words meaning to preserve food in metal containers, can and tin

explanation.surface: Instructions to bottle something twice over, then a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Twice asks for two different synonyms, not the same one doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantina is a Spanish-style bar or canteen serving drinks.

clue.text: Agents apprehending City type

indicators.note: to apprehend is to seize and hold, so the agents close around the next piece

parts.note: EC is the postal district of the City of London

explanation.surface: Secret agents arresting a certain kind of City financier.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcode begins EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a kind or sort, the basic category used to classify organisms.

clue.text: Beneficiary of agreement during exercise

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the agreement sits inside the exercise

explanation.surface: Someone who benefits from a deal struck in the middle of a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: A payee is the person to whom money is paid, so the recipient of funds.

clue.text: Disguised in part of Cartesian dictum without point

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the dictum word goes around the point

parts.note: Descartes wrote cogito ergo sum, I think therefore I am
north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Masked, inside a fragment of Descartes's philosophy that lacks a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' seems to mean lacking, but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone travelling incognito hides their true identity, concealed from recognition.

clue.text: Unknown poet in charge in state is in all the anthologies

indicators.note: in places the previous pieces inside the one that follows

parts.note: anonymous, the attribution for a poem of unknown authorship

explanation.surface: An anonymous verse in charge of a state, found in every collection.
explanation.walkthrough: Unknown poet fits the surface neatly: anonymous poems turn up in every anthology. The state is California.
explanation.definitionFit: Work accepted into the literary canon is regarded as standard, so it gets reprinted in every collection.

clue.text: Take sailors to court about North European of inferior rank

indicators.note: about means around here, so the word for court surrounds the European

parts.note: a native of a Baltic state

explanation.surface: Suing a crew of seamen over a low-ranking Scandinavian.
explanation.walkthrough: Take just tells us to add the sailors, and they go at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective subaltern means subordinate or lower in status; as a noun it is a junior army officer.

clue.text: Used teeth on one bird or another

explanation.surface: Someone sinking their teeth into a bird, or perhaps a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: Another means another bird, so the second piece is itself a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a wading heron of reedbeds, known for its booming call.

clue.text: Vulgar rendition of soul hit

indicators.note: a rendition is a fresh performance or version, so the letters are rendered in a new order

explanation.surface: A crude cover version of a soul chart-topper.
explanation.definitionFit: Loutish behaviour is coarse and ill-mannered, like that of a lout or yob.

clue.text: Apocryphal book, the first with death notice

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word just before it

explanation.surface: A book of the Apocrypha that opens with someone's obituary.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Tobit is one of the Apocrypha, included in Catholic Bibles but not in Protestant canons.

clue.text: Graduates tucked into Mexican snack — it's hot stuff!

indicators.note: tucked into means placed snugly inside, so the graduates go within the snack

explanation.surface: Students tucking into tacos with plenty of hot sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a fiery pepper sauce, a spicy condiment from Louisiana.

clue.text: Cows — that's admitted by their mates

indicators.note: to be admitted is to be let inside, so the phrase goes within the mates

parts.note: i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Cattle and their bovine partners in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: Cows looks like a noun for cattle, which their mates suggests too, but it is the verb meaning intimidates.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them, which is what a bully does to victims.

clue.text: Push out redundant artist missing 4

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the following word is taken away from the first

parts.note: the answer to 4 down, in its sense of coarse

explanation.surface: An unwanted painter left lacking something.
explanation.walkthrough: EXTRA without RA leaves EXT; 4 is GROSS, whose synonym RUDE completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrude is to force material out through an opening, as with pasta or metal.

clue.text: Confer on purpose with old women

explanation.surface: Deliberately discussing matters with elderly ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confer on' reads as a phrasal verb, but on purpose is a phrase too; Confer alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to bestow or grant a gift, quality or funding.

clue.text: "Misty Blue" ran amok

indicators.note: running amok is out of control, so the letters break formation

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the quotation mark

explanation.surface: The song Misty Blue running wild.
explanation.walkthrough: Misty Blue is a song title, which hides that Misty is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebular relates to nebulae, clouds of interstellar gas, so it suggests something cloudy or hazy.

clue.text: (and 26) Will windows provide a solution to children's classic?

parts.note: surface reading: a question about whether panes of glass could solve a problem
setter's reading: the title read as an instruction, putting one word inside another, produces these two words

explanation.surface: Wondering whether windows could crack a puzzle about a classic book.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the full title, with 26, as an instruction: put WIND in WILLOWS, after WILL, and you get 'Will windows'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenneth Grahame's 1908 tale of Mole, Ratty, Badger and Toad is a much-loved children's classic.

clue.text: Copper quietly taking charge of shock absorber

parts.note: an ion is a charged particle, taking on charge

explanation.surface: A policeman discreetly assuming command of a car part.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushion softens impact, absorbing blows the way a padded pillow does.

clue.text: See 24
